subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram provider intermittently stalls despite stable direct Bot API connectivity

question: Should OpenClaw fix this Telegram SOCKS5 stall by changing the shared proxy-agent scheme policy across both explicit and env proxy paths, or wait for stronger live proof before changing proxy behavior?
rationale: The source and Undici contract support the suspected SOCKS failure, but the repair changes a shared compatibility-sensitive proxy helper and the open candidate PR does not yet cover every proxy route with real Telegram proof.

options.title: Repair shared proxy scheme handling
options.body: Update the shared proxy helper so explicit and env HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS proxy routes preserve scheme semantics, then require focused tests and redacted live Telegram SOCKS5 proof before landing.

options.title: Land an explicit-only fix
options.body: Accept a narrower Telegram explicit-proxy repair while leaving env-proxy behavior as a known follow-up risk.

options.title: Wait for live reproduction
options.body: Keep code unchanged until a maintainer or reporter supplies a current-main live SOCKS5 getMe/sendMessage failure and after-fix proof.

recommendation.title: Repair shared proxy scheme handling
recommendation.body: Update the shared proxy helper so explicit and env HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS proxy routes preserve scheme semantics, then require focused tests and redacted live Telegram SOCKS5 proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice centers on the shared HTTP/1.1 proxy dispatcher helper and recent Telegram proxy/liveness history where steipete has the strongest merged-code trail.
